extracted.intended_audience: Prussian/German secondary-education policymakers, gymnasium teachers, university professors concerned with curriculum reform
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and concrete curricular standards for reforming the classical (gymnasium) secondary-school curriculum so it better prepares pupils for modern science, medicine, practical professions, and preserves humanistic ideals without pedantry.

rubrics_metrics.name: More mathematics (increase hours and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematical course must include the discussion of equations of the second degree, a few other plane curves, and must also give an introduction to differential calculus through the theory of tangents; a greater number of hours must be given to mathematics — six or eight, instead of four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics should really stand on an equality with the ancient languages and history in examinations; the equality of the teacher of mathematics with teachers of other branches should be made actual. Analytical methods illuminate many fields (representation of functions by curves, applications in physiology, meteorology, political economy). The omission of analytical geometry from the gymnasium programme is a serious error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach analytical geometry and conic sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical geometry (including conic sections and plane curves) should be included in the gymnasium course; the ministerial exclusion of conic sections is mistaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical geometry opens the way to differential and integral calculus and is often more suitable for philosophically inclined minds than long trigonometrical calculations; many current gymnasium masters are qualified and willing to teach it; some non-Prussian gymnasia already teach it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce foundations of differential calculus
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an introduction to differential calculus (through theory of tangents) within the gymnasium mathematical curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This introduction readies students for later advanced mathematical aims and is pedagogically appropriate when analytical geometry is taught; it is valuable even for medical and physiological studies where graphical methods are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give mathematics equal weight in exams and status of teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examinations for advancement and graduation, mathematics must really stand on an equality with the ancient languages and history; the teacher of mathematics should have equality of rank with other branch teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevation of status and exam weight will make mathematical instruction effective and attract proper emphasis in schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural history in lower classes to awaken observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide enough natural history in the lower classes to awaken the faculty of observing and to familiarize pupils with the method of classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is rooted in the understanding and has great educative force (Cuvier). This is not an extensive scientific conversion but a practical measure to cultivate observational habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach mechanics, astronomy, and mathematical/physical geography in higher classes
rubrics_metrics.description: In the higher classes teach mechanics, the elements of astronomy, and mathematical and physical geography — adding, if necessary, one hour more than heretofore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not aim to convert the gymnasium into a school for science-teaching with full experimental physics/chemistry, but include these elements so pupils headed for architecture, military service, or medicine receive fitting preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude Darwinism from gymnasium instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude Darwinism from what is taught in the gymnasium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes personal adherence to Darwinism yet recommends its exclusion from the gymnasium curriculum (stated as his position in the address).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free time for new subjects by reducing religious instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain hours (e.g., two in the prima) by doing away with religious instruction that is redundant for confirmed Protestant pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semi-official plan spends disproportionate space on religious instruction while giving little to mathematics; removing or reducing this would free time for mathematics and sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict Greek grammatical exercises; emphasize Greek literature and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict the study of Greek grammatical forms and lessen the burden of Greek composition exercises; aim for acquaintance with Greek myth, history, art, and ideas rather than facility in writing Greek phrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The educational aim of Greek (imbibing Hellenic spirit) can be attained without laborious written exercises; reading Homer and Attic masters, use of translations/preparatory work and demonstrative visual aids are preferable to pedantic composition drills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize Latin for training style and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: For exercising intellectual faculties and developing correctness, precision, and brevity of expression, Latin is a better object of study than Greek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latin's clarity and definiteness of meaning help cultivate good style; excessive Greek study may impair German style. Use Latin to train fundamental properties of good expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen instruction in the mother-tongue (German)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure for pupils more thorough instruction in the mother-tongue to remedy widespread ungrammatical and inelegant German among youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of unsettled orthography and problems in word-formation and sentence construction, special attention must be paid to purity of language, pronunciation, force of expression, brevity, and pointedness of style; this is a national educational defect to be remedied by gymnasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform history teaching: focus on general views and cultural heroes, reduce rote dates
rubrics_metrics.description: In history instruction give more general views of the state of civilization and more fully illustrate heroes of science, literature, and art; reduce loss in unimportant details and memorization of dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace mass of unprofitable dates with knowledge of important constants of nature and broad historical perspective; pupils should learn the significance of civilizations and cultural achievement rather than rote party struggles or minor succession dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use demonstratio ad oculos (visual/material aids) in classical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ visual aids and copies of antique works of art to help pupils imbibe the Hellenic spirit rather than relying solely on grammatical drills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrative methods (seeing copies of antique art) can often produce better appreciation of antiquity than prolonged attention to aorist, subjunctive, and particles; broaden pedagogical methods to include visual/cultural materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform the gymnasium's purpose to fit modern requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacrifice some time-honored but antiquated claims so the gymnasium will fit pupils for university, industrial or architectural academy, the army, and other modern careers — not only for intellectual sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transformed gymnasium harmonized with the period and embracing elements of modern civilization will be better able to resist the encroachments of realism; by yielding somewhat it will defend and preserve German idealism more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid purely mechanical examinations that gloss over defective scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that maturity/examination procedures do not mechanically gloss over deficiencies (e.g., students who pass but later cannot trace Greek technical terms to their source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of defective scholarship (poor Latin/Greek vocabularies, lack of historical sense) suggests examinations have been satisfied by mechanical contrivance; reform examination standards to test real mastery and understanding.
